reason: E1 states that HEA surface heterogeneity provides neighboring sites with different electronic structures, enabling tuning of selectivity, and cites IrOsPtPdRhRu as catalyzing a 12-electron ethanol oxidation process. However, E1 provides no evidence for a Gaussian distribution of adsorption energies, the specific dual-site mechanism, or the effect of annealing on heterogeneity and performance; these mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Random alloying in HEAs creates a broad, Gaussian distribution of adsorption energies via the ligand effect
This distribution yields complementary sites: some bind ethanol/intermediates strongly, others weakly
The cooperative dual-site effect enables the 12-electron ethanol oxidation pathway
Thermal annealing reduces local electronic heterogeneity by promoting chemical ordering/segregation
Reducing heterogeneity diminishes the dual-site effect, lowering activity and shifting selectivity to partial oxidation products
